title: Exact completed scalar realization and ordinary balanced pullback
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subset R$ an ideal, and $g:T'\to T$ any scheme morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $\underline N_W$ for constant module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $B_W=\varprojlim_n\underline{R/I^n}_W$, with canonical constant scalar maps and quotient projections [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], for $W=T,T'$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the canonical constant-section comparisons for $g^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].

The constant-section direct-image maps for the rings $R/I^n$ commute with all quotient maps. Their limits define a unique ring-sheaf map $B_T\to g_*B_{T'}$ with those projections. Its adjoint $c_g:g^{-1}B_T\to B_{T'}$ agrees with the projection-induced map, and the square of constant scalar maps from $\underline R_{T'}\cong g^{-1}\underline R_T$ commutes. The module direct image along this map is a right adjoint. Its left adjoint is ordinary ringed pullback $g_B^*F=B_{T'}\otimes_{g^{-1}B_T}g^{-1}F$. These assertions hold in independently enlarged site and coefficient universes satisfying the smallness convention [def-weil-size-convention].

The functor $S_W:N\mapsto B_W\otimes_{\underline R_W}\underline N_W$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] on all $R$-modules is additive and exact. For every cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of $R$-modules, it induces the canonical natural isomorphism
$$\mathcal H^j(S_W(P^\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}S_W(H^j(P^\bullet))$$
for all $j\in\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], induced by the cycle and boundary identifications. For every $R$-module $N$, with no finiteness assumption, there is a natural isomorphism of sheaves
$$g_B^*S_T(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{T'}(N).$$
After the canonical inverse-image constant-module and tensor comparisons, its balanced-tensor formulas are $b'\otimes(b\otimes n)\mapsto b'c_g(b)\otimes n$ and $b'\otimes n\mapsto b'\otimes(1\otimes n)$. They are well-defined mutually inverse sheaf morphisms and are natural in every $R$-linear map $N\to N'$. No flatness of $B_{T'}$ over $g^{-1}B_T$ and no identification of those two rings is asserted.

proof.text: Put $Q_n=R/I^n$, write $q_{mn}:Q_m\to Q_n$ for $m\geq n$, and let $\rho_A:\underline A_T\to g_*\underline A_{T'}$ be the constant-section map of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For every ring homomorphism $a:A\to A'$, the maps $g_*\underline a\circ\rho_A$ and $\rho_{A'}\circ\underline a$ agree: after precomposition with the constant-presheaf sheafification unit both send a scalar $x$ to the constant section $a(x)$, so uniqueness in sheafification makes them equal. Apply this to $q_{mn}$ and to $R\to Q_n$. The canonical isomorphism $g^{-1}\underline R_T\cong\underline R_{T'}$ is that of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], which preserves constant scalars; its adjunct is $\rho_R$ by the same uniqueness argument.

source.place: Tags 093J (constant sheaves) and 03D2 (lemma-pullback-module); constant-section naturality from the sheafification unit

proof.text:
Write $\pi_{W,n}:B_W\to\underline{Q_n}_W$. By the sectionwise inverse-limit description [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], on every site object $U$ one has $(g_*B_{T'})(U)=\lim_n\underline{Q_n}_{T'}(u_gU)$. Thus the compatible maps $\rho_{Q_n}\circ\pi_{T,n}$ define a ring-sheaf map $d_g:B_T\to g_*B_{T'}$, uniquely determined by $(g_*\pi_{T',n})d_g=\rho_{Q_n}\pi_{T,n}$. Restrictions and all ring operations commute with this map coordinatewise. Let $c_g$ be its ring-adjunct using [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Adjunction naturality gives
$$\pi_{T',n}c_g=c_{Q_n}\,g^{-1}(\pi_{T,n}),$$
where $c_{Q_n}$ is the adjunct of $\rho_{Q_n}$. Hence it is exactly the projection-induced map; uniqueness is tested by the projections of the target $B_{T'}$. If $\eta_W:\underline R_W\to B_W$ is the scalar map, each projection of $d_g\eta_T$ is that of $g_*\eta_{T'}\rho_R$ by step 1. These maps are equal by coordinatewise uniqueness. Taking adjuncts yields $c_g g^{-1}(\eta_T)=\eta_{T'}c_R$, the required scalar square.

source.place: Tags 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits) and 03CO (lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves), sectionwise limit; ring adjunction and projection calculation

proof.text: The geometric morphism of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], equipped with $c_g$, satisfies exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Apply its natural Hom bijection with source ring $B_T$ and target ring $B_{T'}$. It identifies the direct image with its action through $d_g$ as a right adjoint, whose left adjoint is $F\mapsto B_{T'}\otimes_{g^{-1}B_T}g^{-1}F$. No condition on $c_g$ other than being a ring map occurs in that theorem.

For each $W$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-algebra-flat-quotients] with $A=R$, ideal $I$, and the identity presentation $S=B_W$. Its map $c$ is $\eta_W$ because its composites are the quotient projections. Its indexing $n+1$ gives the same positive-power tower (including a zeroth quotient would merely add its forced zero coordinate). The hypotheses are precisely that $R$ is commutative Noetherian; neither $I$ nor a module has further restrictions. It states that extension along $\eta_W$ is exact. Compose with the exact constant module functor of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact], whose statement applies to every module despite its title. The composite is $S_W$. It is additive by [def-sfb-flat-scalar-realization] and preserves finite limits and finite colimits as the composite of two such functors. This proves exactness on all $R$-modules.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to the additive exact functor $S_W$ established in step 4 and the arbitrary complex $P^\bullet$. It gives $\mathcal H^j(S_WP^\bullet)\cong S_W(H^jP^\bullet)$ for every integer $j$, natural in chain maps. The cited statement explicitly identifies cycles with $S_W(\ker d^j)$ and boundaries with $S_W(\operatorname{im}d^{j-1})$, and specifies compatibility with their inclusions and quotient projections. Thus its isomorphism is the canonical one required here; boundedness is not used.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, on cycles, boundaries and their quotient

proof.text: Use the ordinary inverse-image/scalar comparison $\chi_g^{AB}$ of [lem-sfb-scalar-inverse-image-tower-diagram] for $A=\underline R_T$, $B=B_T$ (take the third ring there to be $B_T$ with identity map). This identifies $g^{-1}(B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline N_T)$ with $g^{-1}B_T\otimes_{g^{-1}\underline R_T}g^{-1}\underline N_T$, including its actual coefficient action. By [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module], $g^{-1}\underline N_T\cong\underline N_{T'}$ canonically and naturally for every module $N$. Under the constant-ring identification of step 1, set $A=\underline R_{T'}$, $C=g^{-1}B_T$, $D=B_{T'}$, and $M=\underline N_{T'}$. The scalar square in step 2 makes $A\to C\xrightarrow{c_g}D$ equal to the given scalar map $A\to D$. Consequently the pullback in step 3 is canonically $D\otimes_C(C\otimes_A M)$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, ordinary inverse image of the balanced coequalizer

proof.text:
On the tensors of step 6 define $\Phi(d\otimes(c\otimes m))=d\,c_g(c)\otimes m$ and $\Psi(d\otimes m)=d\otimes(1\otimes m)$. These descend by the sheafified tensor universal property [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Indeed the inner $A$-relation $ca\otimes m=c\otimes am$ is respected since $c_g(ca)=c_g(c)\eta_{T'}(a)$; the outer $C$-relation is respected since $dc_g(c_0)c_g(c)=dc_g(c_0c)$. For $\Psi$, the $A$-relation follows from
$$d\eta_{T'}(a)\otimes(1\otimes m)=d\otimes(a\otimes m)=d\otimes(1\otimes am).$$
Both rules are additive and $D$-linear and commute with restrictions. Thus the presheaf balanced pairings extend uniquely to sheaf morphisms, also when sections of the tensor sheaf are only locally represented by sums of pure tensors. On local pure tensors $\Phi\Psi(d\otimes m)=d\otimes m$, and
$$\Psi\Phi(d\otimes(c\otimes m))=dc_g(c)\otimes(1\otimes m)=d\otimes(c\otimes m).$$
Their composites are identities by the same universal property. A linear map $h:N\to N'$ replaces $m$ by $\underline h(m)$ in both formulas, so both squares commute. With step 6 this proves the specified natural pullback isomorphism for every $N$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: bilinear universal property; explicit scalar balancing and inverse calculation

proof.text: Choose a common ambient universe containing the two site skeletons, the coefficient ring, the countable towers and all modules in question, as in [def-weil-size-convention]. The adjunction node in step 3 and the geometric constant-module node in step 6 require only that the sites be small in that ambient coefficient universe. These conditions hold after independently enlarging the site and coefficient universes subject to this convention. The limit construction is coordinatewise, flatness in step 4 is supplied for the original site by the cited theorem, and the remaining maps are given by the same constant-section and balanced-tensor formulas. Repeating the argument there proves every assertion in those universes. No step has required preservation of the infinite limit by $g^{-1}$ or flatness of $D$ over $C$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q54-5d06fdc52 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full: 8 steps, no new nodes, statement unchanged. I also read all 13 cited statements and Stacks 093J (lemma-constant-exact), 093M (lemma-completion-flat) and 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback). Step 1: rho_A is the unique sheaf extension in def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, so g_*a∘rho_A=rho_A'∘a, and lem-pe's scalar-preserving isomorphism equals c_R. Step 2: g_* and the limit are both sectionwise, so d_g is unique; the adjunct computation pi'_n c_g = c_{Q_n} g^{-1}pi_n is correct, and the scalar square follows from step 1. g^{-1} is never claimed to commute with the limit. Step 3: ringed-topoi-module-adjunction takes arbitrary commutative R,S and a ring map, with no flatness, matching g_B^*. Step 4: the flat-quotients node (Noetherian A, any I, n+1 indexing is the same tower, c=eta_W) and finite-type-constant-exact (constant functor exact on all modules) compose to S_W, the same construction as def-sfb-flat-scalar-realization. Step 5: exact-functor-complex-cohomology has no boundedness and gives the cycle/boundary identification. Step 6: chi of scalar-inverse-image-tower-diagram (A=R_T, B=C=B_T) plus geometric-inverse-image-constant-module (any N, natural) gives D⊗_C(C⊗_A M). Step 7: I checked the Phi/Psi balancing relations, including c_g(ca)=c_g(c)eta(a) from the step-2 square, and both composites on local pure tensors; this is elementary. Step 8: size conditions are only smallness of the sites. Edge cases I=0, I=R, zero ring, N=0, infinite free N, g=id and empty T all hold, and finite presentation of N is never needed. Duplicate check: lem-sfb-admissible-scalar-realization-exact covers only special condensed Lambda; completed-constant-sheaf-reduction, completed-constant-module-model (finite modules only), lem-tw-ordinary-completed-integral-pullback (derived completion comparison) and coefficient-pullback-linearity (automorphisms) are not duplicates. No cycle and no SGA. I accept the 8 generic tool_uses listed in split_report. No fixes.
